update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency British Governor-Generals and Viceroys and their major historical events for History Static GK.

governor_generals_of_bengal.name: Warren Hastings
key_events_and_reforms: First Governor-General of Bengal.
End of Dual Government in Bengal.
Regulating Act of 1773 and Pitt's India Act of 1784.
Foundation of the Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784) with William Jones.

governor_generals_of_bengal.name: Lord Cornwallis
key_events_and_reforms: Introduction of the Permanent Settlement in Bengal and Bihar (1793).
Known as the 'Father of Civil Services in India'.
Introduction of the Cornwallis Code (separation of revenue and justice administration).

governor_generals_of_bengal.name: Lord Wellesley
key_events_and_reforms: Introduction of the Subsidiary Alliance system (Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to sign).
Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799) and death of Tipu Sultan.
Establishment of Fort William College at Calcutta.

governor_generals_of_india.name: Lord William Bentinck
key_events_and_reforms: First Governor-General of India (Charter Act of 1833).
Abolition of Sati (1829) with the help of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
Suppression of Thuggee (1830).
Introduction of English as the official language of higher education (Macaulay's Minute, 1835).

governor_generals_of_india.name: Lord Dalhousie
key_events_and_reforms: Introduction of the Doctrine of Lapse (Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur annexed).
Introduction of the first Railway line connecting Bombay and Thane (1853).
Establishment of the electric telegraph and modern postal system.
Wood's Despatch on Education (1854), known as the Magna Carta of English education in India.

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Canning
key_events_and_reforms: Last Governor-General and First Viceroy of India.
Revolt of 1857 (Sepoy Mutiny) occurred during his tenure.
Government of India Act 1858 (Company rule ended, Crown rule began).
Establishment of Universities at Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras (1857).

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Lytton
key_events_and_reforms: Passed the Vernacular Press Act (1878) and Arms Act (1878).
Organized the Grand Delhi Durbar (1877) when Queen Victoria assumed the title 'Kaiser-i-Hind'.
Highly unpopular for his handling of the Great Famine of 1876-1878.

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Ripon
key_events_and_reforms: Known as the most liberal and popular Viceroy.
Repeal of the Vernacular Press Act (1882).
Resolution on Local Self-Government (1882) - 'Father of Local Self-Government'.
Appointment of the Hunter Commission on Education (1882).
Ilbert Bill controversy (1883-1884).

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Curzon
key_events_and_reforms: Partition of Bengal (1905), which triggered the Swadeshi Movement.
Passed the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act (1904).
Established the Department of Agriculture and the Archaeological Survey of India.

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Minto II
key_events_and_reforms: Swadeshi Movement continued.
Surat Split of the Indian National Congress (1907).
Establishment of the Muslim League (1906).
Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Chelmsford
key_events_and_reforms: Lucknow Pact (1916) between Congress and Muslim League.
Passing of the Rowlatt Act (1919) and the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919).
Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced dyarchy in provinces.
Launch of the Non-Cooperation and Khilafat Movements.

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Irwin
key_events_and_reforms: Arrival of the Simon Commission (1928) and subsequent boycotts.
Purna Swaraj resolution passed at Lahore Session (1929).
Dandi March and launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930).
Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Linlithgow
key_events_and_reforms: Longest tenure as Viceroy.
Outbreak of World War II (1939) and resignation of Congress ministries.
August Offer (1940) and Cripps Mission (1942).
Launch of the Quit India Movement (1942).

viceroys_of_india.name: Lord Mountbatten
key_events_and_reforms: Last Viceroy of British India and First Governor-General of Independent India.
Proposed the Mountbatten Plan (June 3 Plan) for the partition of India.
Passed the Indian Independence Act (1947).

viceroys_of_india.name: Chakravarti Rajagopalachari
key_events_and_reforms: The first and only Indian to hold the post of Governor-General of India.
Served until India became a Republic on January 26, 1950, after which the post was abolished.
